home.hero.paragraph: FortCloud turns the story you tell about your infrastructure into versioned models, readable checks and evidence your team can actually discuss — without sending your diagrams or credentials anywhere.
home.hero.trust.noCredentials: No cloud credentials in the browser
home.loop.title: The quiet loop
home.why.paragraph: Diagrams age. Runbooks drift. A green dashboard rarely explains what happens when a region disappears. FortCloud keeps the decision close to the code: a model you can review, a check you can run and a report that can be questioned in a pull request.
home.principle.1.title: Make the story explicit
home.principle.1.body: Resilience usually lives in slides and headings. FortCloud moves it into small, versioned files where intent, ownership and trade-offs can be read by a human.
home.principle.2.title: Review the decision, not the syntax
home.principle.2.body: Scenarios and staged imports show exactly what changed. A reviewer can discuss the risk itself — not guess what a dashboard snapshot was supposed to mean.
home.principle.3.title: Regenerate evidence on demand
home.principle.3.body: Graphs, matrices and status files are rebuilt from the model by check. No hand-maintained report can drift away from the thing it claims to describe.
home.who.headline.start: For the people who answer when someone asks:
home.who.paragraph: You do not need a resilience platform or a dedicated tooling team. You need a calm way to state intent, keep it current and show the work. Each tool can be adopted on its own.
home.audience.1.title: Platform & architecture teams
home.audience.1.body: See the shape of a system before a redesign, and keep the reasoning next to the diagrams.
home.audience.2.title: SRE & reliability engineers
home.audience.2.body: Turn failover, restore and latency promises into checks that fail loudly in CI.
home.audience.3.title: Security & compliance leads
home.audience.3.body: Show least privilege, auditable changes and dated evidence without another spreadsheet.
home.audience.4.title: Teams without a platform budget
home.audience.4.body: Start with one tool and one service. No backend, no agent, no new platform to adopt.
home.tools.headline: Seven focused tools. One quiet discipline.
home.tools.paragraph: Each tool answers one uncomfortable question and produces its own evidence. Start with the question you cannot currently answer.
home.tool.atlas.question: Where is the risk, and what is the blast radius?
home.tool.atlas.detail: Atlas draws the system as a graph, then names the single points of failure, single-region P0s and uncovered resilience promises hiding inside it.
home.tool.failover.question: Could we really switch over in time?
home.tool.failover.detail: Failover checks that every critical service has a real standby, a detection path, a promotion plan, enough capacity and a drill recent enough to trust.
home.tool.ark.question: Do our restores actually work?
home.tool.ark.detail: Ark treats backup as a claim that needs evidence. It checks coverage, immutability, retention and dated restore tests instead of accepting a green checkbox.
home.tool.ballast.question: What happens to latency when a dependency fails?
home.tool.ballast.detail: Ballast adds up the worst-case timeout budget, then checks retries, breakers, bulkheads and fallbacks so a slow call cannot quietly take down the chain.
home.tool.vitals.question: Would we see a breach early enough?
home.tool.vitals.detail: Vitals connects signals, SLOs and verification checks. It keeps objectives honest, alert thresholds meaningful and data quality visible beside uptime.
home.tool.custodian.question: Can we prove who changed what, and why?
home.tool.custodian.detail: Custodian keeps access least-privileged, secrets referenced rather than copied, audit sinks immutable and every production change reviewable and reversible.
home.tool.crucible.question: Have we rehearsed the outage?
home.tool.crucible.detail: Crucible plans controlled failure drills with four clear roles, communication cadence and verified outcomes — before the real incident writes the script.
home.tool.fallback.question: What does this tool help us prove?
home.tool.fallback.detail: A focused model, a readable check and evidence your team can review together.
home.rhythm.headline: Declare. Review. Prove. Repeat.
home.rhythm.paragraph: The console is deliberately a consumer of the tools. It makes the model easier to write and the evidence easier to read — it never becomes another system of record.
home.rhythm.step.1.title: Describe
home.rhythm.step.1.body: Use the guided form or edit YAML directly. The model stays local and readable.
home.rhythm.step.2.title: Propose
home.rhythm.step.2.body: Optional AWS, Azure and GCP connectors suggest an inventory from non-secret identifiers only.
home.rhythm.step.3.title: Review
home.rhythm.step.3.body: Read the diff, create a scenario, accept or discard. Nothing is applied silently.
home.rhythm.step.4.title: Prove
home.rhythm.step.4.body: Run check locally or in CI. Reports and status files are rebuilt from the model.
home.final.headline: Start with one uncomfortable question.
home.final.paragraph: If you do not know where to begin, open Atlas with one production service. It will show you the risk before the next incident does.
home.footer.local: Local console · models stay in web/workspaces/
